# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

I can see the bomb’s current state: the display reads 0, the indicator light is red, and the three wires are yellow, green, and red in positions 1, 2, and 3. I am relaying all of this to the Blind so they can compare it with the manual instructions. The long gesture sequence from the Mute is visible to me, but without the manual I cannot determine its meaning; the Blind’s gesture was a pointing signal.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display 0. Indicator light red. Wires: position 1 yellow, position 2 green, position 3 red.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I cannot determine the meaning of your gesture sequence without the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb has not changed: display 0, red light, and wires yellow, green, red in positions 1–3. The Mute’s new visible sequence differs from the previous one: it uses 👌 at the first, second, and third separator-like locations, with ✋ at the other two. Since the Blind cannot see these gestures, I will describe the complete sequence and both rounds so the manual can be applied to it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute gesture sequence this round, in order: ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝. Previous round was: ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝. Bomb remains display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. The Mute has now sent a single gesture, ✌, which I can see but cannot interpret without the manual. I will identify it explicitly to the Blind, who may be able to match it against the manual and determine the required operation. I will also repeat the bomb state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent one gesture: ✌, the victory-hand sign. Bomb still reads display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the Mute again sent only ✌. I cannot safely assign an operational meaning to that sign; I will relay its exact identity to the Blind rather than guess. No action should be taken until the manual’s instruction is identified.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 4: Mute again sent exactly one gesture, ✌. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I cannot safely interpret ✌ as an action.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. The Mute has again sent exactly one ✌ gesture; this is now the third consecutive turn with that same signal. I will report the repetition to the Blind, while avoiding an unsafe interpretation or action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 5: Mute again sent exactly one ✌ (two-finger victory sign); this is the third consecutive turn with only ✌. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]

The bomb is still unchanged: display 0, red light, and wires yellow, green, red in positions 1–3. The Mute now sent two consecutive ✌ gestures, rather than one. I will relay the exact sequence and current bomb state to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 6: Mute sent exactly two gestures: ✌ ✌. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb has changed, confirming that the correct wire was cut: wire 2, previously green, is now cut. The indicator light is now blue while the display remains 0; wires 1 and 3 remain yellow and red. The Mute sent 👎, whose meaning I cannot infer safely, so I am relaying the exact visible facts to both teammates.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The system confirms the correct wire was cut. Current bomb: display 0, light blue, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 CUT, wire 3 red. Mute sent one gesture: 👎.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the correct wire was cut: wire 2 is now CUT. Current display 0, light blue; wires 1 yellow and 3 red. I saw your gesture 👎.")
wait()
```
